change: Native daemon ownership checks now require proof that the legacy Python Keeper process has exited, even if the daemon lease is absent/unmounted or Keeper record says stopped. No legacy process is killed or legacy metadata rewritten.
limits: PID-only legacy records cannot distinguish reuse. A live reused PID or access-denied observation remains fenced and requires explicit migration/retirement of legacy metadata.
The check does not stop an unmodified external writer from editing files or racing a new launch; production cutover still requires confirmed legacy shutdown.
No production Herdr controls or account PATH changes. No claim of a new full regression.
